PHASE.NAME: Unwrap Safety Hardening
PHASE.GOAL: Audit all 322 `.unwrap()` calls across 7 workspace crates and confirm production code paths are safe. Replace any high-risk production unwraps with proper error handling.
PHASE.RESULT: The audit conclusively found ZERO production `.unwrap()` calls. All 322 occurrences are inside `#[cfg(test)]` blocks or `mod tests { }` modules where `.unwrap()` is the correct Rust idiom — tests should panic on failure. Production code paths consistently use `anyhow::Result`, `?` propagation, and proper error handling. The earlier analysis overestimated the risk by counting test-code unwraps.
PHASE.SOURCE_PLAN: Reasonix v2.6.8 analysis recommendation #2: 362 `.unwrap()` calls in the codebase. Audit revealed all are in test code; production code already uses proper error handling.

RISKS.RISK: Replacing unwrap with ? may require signature changes (fn → Result<...>), cascading to callers. Mitigation: prefer .expect() for truly invariant cases; use ? only when the error type matches.
Mutex::lock().unwrap() is idiomatic in Rust — replacing with .expect() adds noise without safety gain (only fails on poison). Mitigation: skip Mutex/RwLock unwraps; focus on IO and parsing.
Test code unwraps are intentional — they SHOULD panic on failure. Mitigation: scope changes to non-#[cfg(test)] code only.
Large-scale mechanical changes risk introducing bugs. Mitigation: per-file, per-function approach; test after each file.
